title: ChatGPT in higher education: Opportunities, challenges, and required competencies in the absence of guiding policies
venue: Journal of Education and e-Learning Research
extended_summary:
This paper examines how ChatGPT is being used in higher education and what opportunities, challenges, and user competencies are associated with its adoption in the absence of formal institutional policies. The study asks how faculty and students perceive ChatGPT, what kinds of tasks they use it for, and what risks emerge when its use is not clearly governed.

The authors conducted a qualitative case study at a federal university in the United Arab Emirates. Data came from semi-structured interviews with 10 faculty members and 10 students, plus documentation of live ChatGPT use and other participant-shared materials. Participants included undergraduate and graduate students and teachers across several colleges. The analysis focused on thematic patterns in how ChatGPT was used for writing support, lesson planning, information seeking, editing, and other academic tasks.

Findings suggest that ChatGPT is viewed as time-saving, cost-effective, adaptable, and useful for personalized support, but it also raises concerns about overreliance, misinformation, plagiarism, and unclear boundaries for appropriate use. A major conclusion is that effective use depends on prompt engineering and critical evaluation skills, and that universities need clearer policies, targeted training, and more explicit curricular guidance to separate legitimate pedagogical support from misuse or academic dishonesty.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative case study with interviews and document triangulation, which provides useful contextual evidence but not causal estimates. It is peer-reviewed and methodologically described, but it does not meet stronger experimental or quasi-experimental credibility criteria.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports perceived benefits such as time savings and improved support, but provides no quantitative effect sizes or outcome gains. Its impact is therefore meaningful but unclear in magnitude for general or priority populations.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT used by university students and faculty as a conversational AI for answering questions, generating explanations, brainstorming ideas, summarizing content, drafting materials, and providing tailored learning support in higher education.

finding.finding_summary: Participants unanimously reported that ChatGPT saved time and money on coursework and teaching tasks. In interviews with 10 faculty and 10 students, it was described as a time-saver for proofreading, editing, revising proposals, creating lesson plans, and preparing presentations; no quantitative effect size was reported.
finding.measure: Perceived time savings, cost-effectiveness, and workflow efficiency from interviews

finding.finding_summary: Participants said ChatGPT could support understanding and problem solving when used well, especially when prompts were carefully engineered, but they also worried it could weaken critical thinking through overreliance and addiction. The study is qualitative, so it reports perceptions rather than a numerical effect size.
finding.measure: Perceived critical thinking, prompt engineering competency, and dependence/addiction themes from interviews

finding.finding_summary: ChatGPT was viewed as helpful for writing-related tasks such as drafting, proofreading, editing, and revising assignments, but it also raised major concerns about plagiarism and reduced originality. The study involved 10 faculty and 10 students and reported qualitative themes only, with no effect size.
finding.measure: Perceived writing support, proofreading/editing, and plagiarism concerns

finding.finding_summary: Participants described ChatGPT as useful for explaining mathematical content and solving problems, but also reported incorrect answers and fabricated reasoning in some cases. No quantitative achievement data were reported; evidence is based on interview narratives from 20 participants.
finding.measure: Perceived support for math problem solving and reported accuracy failures on math tasks

finding.finding_summary: Students reported that ChatGPT could help unpack science concepts such as genetics and biology with simplified explanations, diagrams, and step-by-step support. However, participants also noted hallucinations and incorrect answers, so the study presents a mixed qualitative picture rather than measurable gains.
finding.measure: Perceived support for understanding biology/genetics concepts and accuracy of science-related responses

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that institutions need formal policies, guidelines, and targeted training workshops to govern ChatGPT use responsibly. Participants reported a lack of consensus and inconsistent informal rules across classes, making policy development a central institutional outcome of the study.
finding.measure: Need for institutional policy, governance, and training around ChatGPT use
